analysis.title: INTRADAY U.S. EQUITIES COLOR - 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: GS equities desk says yesterday was one of its busiest days of the year by number of trades and notional executed, while today is the opposite, with many client requests for color and little to see.
The long-only community is described as frozen again. The desk says there was heavy de-risking into the midterms, and traders were surprised by yesterday's move and got pulled back in.
Hedge funds are selling pockets of the market (hyperscalers) that they bought yesterday. The desk sees no buyers stepping in to defend anything yet.
Brokers with heavy retail presence report a second day of very noteworthy sell skews. The desk reads this as top-down pressure applied through macro instruments.
Volumes versus 20-day average: SPY +160%, QQQ +100%, SMH +150%, DRAM +75%.
Semiconductors are under continued pressure on the view that by 2028 there will not be enough data center shells (land, power, shell), leaving too many semiconductors for too few shells.
Acute pressure is also in engineering and construction stocks (data center construction), IPPs and power names (especially with TX, GA and OH exposure), and neoclouds.
Permitting-driven bottleneck concerns in land, power and shell make traders cautious on memory companies (HDDs, DRAM, NAND) that benefited from price (ASP) gains and supply/demand imbalances.

Multiples are contracting meaningfully as investors worry that 2028 gigawatts added could be close to flat y/y with 2027, versus the more than 30% y/y GW (or capex) growth in 2028 that investors had anticipated at the top of the cycle.

Traders are cautious on memory names that gained on higher ASPs and supply/demand imbalances, given shell bottleneck concerns.
Acute pressure in E&C stocks that build data centers.
Acute pressure in IPPs and power names, especially those with TX, GA and OH exposure.

risk_factors: Data center shell shortage (land, power, shell) due to permitting could leave excess semiconductor supply by 2028.
